C08-M01-L06-F1.title: SLA timers on one case: start, stop, pause, warn, breach
C08-M01-L06-F1.caption: How SLA timers start when an alert reaches the queue, stop at acknowledgement and triage, pause only where the SLA allows, and warn before they breach.
C08-M01-L06-F1.alt: Decision graph. Alert reaches SOC queue, where SLA clocks start in UTC, leads to Analyst acknowledges, which stops time to acknowledge. A dashed failure path labelled no owner yet leads from the start to 75% of target elapsed, which warns the owner and shift lead, and a further dashed arrow labelled still no owner leads to Target missed: breach, which escalates and records a reason code. Analyst acknowledges leads to a Triage decision with three branches: benign to Closed: false or benign, where triage and resolve clocks stop; malicious to Escalated as incident, where time to notify starts; and needs customer input to Awaiting customer, where the clock pauses only if the SLA allows. Awaiting customer returns to the triage decision when the reply is received.

nodes.label: Awaiting customer
nodes.sub: clock paused only if SLA allows

C08-M01-L06-F1.note: Every arrow is a timestamped event in the case record; the SLA engine computes elapsed time from those events, minus permitted pauses.

C08-M01-L06-F2.title: Illustrative SOC SLA matrix by severity
C08-M01-L06-F2.caption: The fictional Banyan Microfinance SOC's targets for acknowledgement, triage and customer notification, and the escalation method, at each severity level.
C08-M01-L06-F2.alt: Table with columns Severity, Acknowledge, Triage, Notify customer and Escalation. Critical: 15 min, 30 min, within 1 h of confirmation, phone on-call plus case. High: 30 min, 2 h, within 4 h, case plus chat to shift lead. Medium: 4 h, 1 business day, in daily report, case queue. Low: 1 business day, 3 business days, in weekly report, case queue.
C08-M01-L06-F2.note: Illustrative values for a fictional 24x7 SOC; notification is measured from incident confirmation, the other targets from alert arrival.
